fix.description: A command for `<prefix>_run` that may fix it; never run by the host itself.

details.description: What the kit reports about the document.

draft.description: This is the agent's draft of the file.

description: The arguments (`input`) and structured results (`output`) of every kit tool, as kition-kits-mcp and Kition's agent offer them, generated from crates/kition-kits (`kition-kits-mcp --schemas`). `<prefix>` is the kit's `kit.json` agent prefix. A failed call answers `isError: true` and `error` in its structured content, beside what it had done. `<prefix>_query` and `<prefix>_batch` arguments name the kit's object types and fields once the server has seen its `model.describe`.
title: Kition kit tools (KHP agent tools, `<prefix>_*`)

<prefix>_batch.description: Edit a document in <Kit> through its object model: one model/batch of `ops`, run in order as one undoable step (each run of ops between commands is one transaction; nothing changes when an op fails), then `load` reads objects back. Ops: create {type, fields?, ref?: "$name", in?: "<target>.<field>", at?, parent?}, set {target, field, value}, delete {target}, text.insert {target, field, index, text}, text.delete {target, field, index, count}, text.set {target, field, text}, text.mark/text.unmark {target, field, start, end, key, value?}, list.insert {target, field, item, index?}, list.move {target, field, from, to}, list.remove {target, field, index}, map.set/map.delete {target, field, key, value?}, tree.insert/tree.move {target, field, item, parent?}, command {id, params?}. A target is `root`, an object id from <prefix>_query, or a `$name` bound by an earlier create. Saves the file unless `save` is false; with `draft`, edits your draft instead (never saved). Failures answer `error.code` and the op's `index`. Low level: `text.set` here replaces the text together with its formatting, and created objects get default styles; for ordinary edits prefer the kit's commands (its commands and run tools), which keep formatting.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

load.description: Objects to read after the ops.

in.description: `create`: the list or tree to add it to, as `<target>.<field>`.

ref.description: `create`: a `$name` later ops use for the new object.

save.description: Save the file after the batch. Defaults to true; a draft is never saved.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_check.description: Check a document in <Kit>: lists what the kit finds wrong with it (broken references, overflowing text, formula errors), each with a stable `code`, a `severity` (error, warning, info), its `target` (object id, slide, page, sheet, cell), a message, and sometimes a `fix` command for <prefix>_run. Call it after editing and fix the errors it reports. Changes nothing.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.
Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_commands.description: Search <Kit>'s editing commands (the kit's commands) by keywords. Returns command ids, what each does, and its parameters in one line; pass `detail: true` (or a command id as the query) for the full parameter schema. Without a query it lists every command by id, a page at a time (`cursor`, `limit`). Pass an id to <prefix>_run.

cursor.description: Without a query: the `next` of the previous page.

detail.description: List each command's full parameter and result schemas instead of one line.

limit.description: Without a query: commands a page, at most 200 (default 50).

query.description: Keywords to match in the command id, title, or description, for example `<keywords>`. Leave it out to list every command.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

total.description: How many matched; at most 40 are listed.

<prefix>_create.description: Create a new, empty document in <Kit> at `path` () and save it. The file is always new: when `path` exists the next free name is used. Lists the file it wrote; edit it with the other tools.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the new file, for example `deck.kslide`.

size.description: The document size in pixels, for example {"width": 1920, "height": 1080}.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_draft_ready.description: Ask the person to review your draft of a document in <Kit>: they see a comparison with the document and merge it or discard it. Call it when the draft is done; do not merge or discard it yourself.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_draft_reopen.description: Take your draft of a document in <Kit> back from review to keep editing it (after <prefix>_draft_ready); edits with `draft` also do.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_export.description: Export a document from <Kit> to a new file, as the kit's engine draws it. The file is always new: when `to` exists the next free name is used. Lists the file it wrote; changes nothing in the document.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

format.description: The format, a file extension; defaults to the extension of `to`.

options.description: Parameters for the kit's export command, as <prefix>_commands documents it.

to.description: Workspace-relative path of the new file, for example `exports/Screen.png`.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

version.description: The SHA-256 of the file written.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_inspect.description: Open a document (<formats>) in <Kit> and report the document. By default it also attaches a rendered preview to the next turn so you can see it. With `target` (for example {"slide": 3}) it previews only that part and lists its objects (ids, kinds, names, boxes, text, fills), which is the usual way to find what to edit. Use it before and after editing.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

maxSize.description: The most preview pixels on the longer side.

preview.description: Attach a rendered preview image. Defaults to true.

scale.description: Preview pixels per document unit, up to 2 (default 1), for kits that render previews themselves.

target.description: Look at one part: {"slide": 3} or {"page": 2} (counted from 1) previews it and lists its objects; a diagnostic's `target` from the check tool (for example {"path": "layer:12"}) previews what it is about; {"range": "A1:J20", "sheet": "name"} lists those cells of a spreadsheet; {"paragraphs": [0, 30]} lists those paragraphs of a document (counted from 0). Kits that cannot render a part fall back to the whole document.

details.description: What the kit reports about the document.

document.description: The document, when its open editor answered.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

<prefix>_query.description: Read a document's objects in <Kit> from its object model: by id (`objects`, `root` for the document itself), or by following fields from the root (`follow`, for example `slides` or `slides.0.shapes`). Answers each object's id, type, and fields (all, or those in `fields`). Use the ids with <prefix>_batch. Low level: to find what to edit, the inspect tool with a `target` is usually enough. Call it with `describe: true` first to learn the document's object types and fields.

describe.description: true: also answer the kit's object types and their fields, one line each; a type name or a comma-separated list: those types in full; "*": every type in full and their JSON Schema.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

fields.description: Only these fields of each object. Defaults to all.

follow.description: A field path from the first object (the root by default): field names, and list or tree positions, joined with dots. Reads the objects it ends at.

limit.description: At most this many objects. Defaults to 50.

objects.description: Object ids to read; `root` is the document's root object. Defaults to the root.

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.

items.description: An object as `{ id, type, fields }` read with the fields asked for.

schema.description: With `describe`: the object types as JSON Schema.

<prefix>_run.description: Edit a document in <Kit> by running commands in order, then save the file. Each step is one undoable command with a JSON object of params, as documented by <prefix>_commands. Stops at the first failing step. Answers each step's result and a short document summary. With `draft`, the steps edit your draft of the file instead (never saved); call <prefix>_draft_ready when it is done.

draft.description: Work on your draft of the file instead of the live document: the person reviews it and merges or discards it. Defaults to the run's mode.

preview.description: Attach a rendered preview of the whole document. Defaults to false; use the inspect tool with a target to look at one part.

save.description: Save the file after the steps. Defaults to true; a draft is never saved.

command.description: A command id from <prefix>_commands, for example `<command>`.

target.description: The part the steps act on, as in the inspect tool's target, for example {"slide": 3} (counted from 1). The kit goes there first, so the ids the inspect tool listed for that part work.

completed.description: The steps that ran, in order; on failure, those before the failing one. `changed` is there only when false (the step changed nothing), `result` only when the command answered one.

truncated.description: The result was cut to fit: `shown` of `total` items (of `field` when the result is an object).

draft.description: Edited or read the agent's draft, not the file.

live.description: Edited or read in the file's open editor.
